newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: S. Korean refiners turn aggressive petrol exporters.
newsitem.headline: S. Korean refiners turn aggressive petrol exporters.

text.p: South Korea's refiners have turned into eager petrol exporters, with new capacity boosting available exports by 1.5 million barrels a month, industry sources said on Monday.
"They (refiners) look aggressive because of the oversupply in the domestic market," said Young-Seok Moon, director of petroleum policy division of the Korea Energy Economics Institute.

Ssangyong Oil Refining Co, an affiliate of the Ssangyong Group, exported its first petrol cargo after starting up a new, 40,000-barrel-per-day residue fluid catalytic cracker (RFCC) earlier this month.
RFCCs break up straight-run heavy gas oil with the aid of a catalyst into petrol.
Ssangyong had already sold two gasoline cargoes, totalling up to 400,000-barrels of 95-octane unleaded grade lifting in April for export to Singapore and the Philippines, a company official said.
Industry sources said this would raise South Korean monthly petrol exports by a third, to up to 1.5 million barrels, or six cargoes of around 250,000 barrels each.

They said Yukong Ltd currently exports up to two cargoes a month while one cargo each was available from LG-Caltex, a joint venture between the LG Group, Caltex and Hyundai Oil Refinery Co of the Hyundai Group
Caltex is a joint venture between Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp.

Only one of South Korea's five refiners, Hanwha Energy Co, was still in a short position on petrol and imported one cargo a month, traders said. But it plans to start up its first 40,000-bpd RFCC at the end of the decade.
South Korean petrol exports started hitting the Asia market last year, with some 620,000 bpd of topping capacity brought on stream to bring the country's total refining capacity to 2.438 million bpd.
Petrol exports stood at 2.546 million barrels in 1996 compared to 442,000 barrels in 1995.

The country's largest refiner, Yukong Ltd, brought on stream the country's second RFCC, a 50,000 bpd unit, in September last year and has become an active seller in Taiwan's bi-monthly import tender since February.
Yukong, the first South Korean refiner to export petrol to Japan since it liberalised its oil imports in 1996, plans to increase exports by 100,000 barrels to 700,000 barrels this year.
Some South Korean barrels are heading further afield.

LG-Caltex recently made its first sale to the Middle East, selling an April lifting cargo to state-owned Saudi Aramco, traders said. In February, the refiner clinched the first export deal to the United States.
"But the overcapacity will disappear in the near future, by 2000, and marketing in east Asia is not going to last long," Moon said.
He said domestic demand, currently around 150,000 bpd, was growing at an annual rate of five percent.
